title: Physical-coordinate metric for the conditional gap
question: Does replacing the oscillator level-index edge metric by the physical coordinate spacing produce a more stable conditional coercivity profile, or is the R-400 tail bottleneck intrinsic?

new_perspective.principle: Measure likelihood variation in the physical oscillator coordinate, not in the arbitrary truncation-level label.
motivation: The R-400 birth-death form assigns unit distance to every adjacent eigenlevel, even though the oscillator coordinate spacing changes with the cutoff.
The q-eigenvalues are the coordinates used by the finite Q3 Gibbs law; their shrinking high-level spacing can turn a coordinate-Lipschitz estimate into a stronger level-index coercivity estimate.
The metric change is kept explicit so it cannot be silently identified with the original R-399 form; an analytic comparison to the Hamiltonian-derived common core is a separate gate.
route: Diagonalize the one-site oscillator coordinate q and sort its eigenvalues x_k.
For each conditional law pi_a, form D_q(f)=sum_k min(pi_a(k),pi_a(k+1))*((f(k+1)-f(k))/(x_(k+1)-x_k))^2.
Compute the first nonzero generalized gap for D_q and retain the original level-index gap beside it.
Stress both orientations, every prefix, all declared volumes/cutoffs and beta values, then compare adjacent cutoff ratios for the two metrics.
Require a future theorem comparing the physical-coordinate form to the actual Q3 likelihood gradient before using this route for shell summability.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: A cutoff-stable physical-coordinate conditional form could feed the R-399 shell transfer if a common-core q-Lipschitz estimate is proved. This finite diagnostic supplies neither that comparison nor any OS/KMS/GNS or mass-gap conclusion.

finite_theorem.coordinate_gap: lambda_q is the second eigenvalue of diag(pi)^(-1/2)L_q diag(pi)^(-1/2)
finite_theorem.comparison: The index metric and physical-coordinate metric are reported side by side; no equality or uniform comparison is assumed.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks only scalar positivity of coordinate spacing factors and finite metric ratios; it does not formalize Q3 spectra, coordinate-limit comparison or any continuum statement.

promotion_criteria: Prove a uniform comparison between the physical-coordinate conditional form and the actual Hamiltonian-derived likelihood gradient on a common core.
Prove cutoff-, volume-, phase- and shape-uniform lower control for the coordinate-metric conditional form, including the phase-conditioned case.
Only then combine the coordinate form with R-399 shell weights and pass the regulator limits.
stop_conditions: If the coordinate-metric minimum collapses with the same profile as the index metric, retain R-399 and register this metric rescue as unsuccessful.
If the coordinate metric is stable only for a restricted beta or volume, keep it as a finite fixed-parameter interface and do not promote uniformity.
If no analytic comparison to the Q3 generator can be proved, do not substitute the coordinate form into the shell theorem.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite coordinate-metric cutoff diagnostic. It proves no uniform conditional gap, no Hamiltonian-form comparison, no common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The coordinate metric is a proposed physical reparametrization of a finite one-dimensional form. A larger finite gap than R-400 does not establish a thermodynamic lower bound or a Q3 locality theorem.
